aero.intro: In this step we calculate the 3D wing lift slope (CLα), zero-lift drag (CD0) and induced drag factor (k). These coefficients determine the aircraft's L/D performance and the total drag the motor must overcome in cruise. The safety of the aircraft flying without stalling is guaranteed by the drag polar curve here.
aero.out.cd0_total.desc: Drag due to fuselage, wing and tail at zero lift. Determines power consumption at high speed.
aero.out.cl_max_3d.desc: Maximum lift coefficient the 3D wing can produce before stalling (0.9 × Cl_max_2d). Sets the lower limit of stall speed.
aero.out.cl_range_cl_end.desc: Characteristic lift coefficients for best range and longest endurance cruise speeds.
aero.out.cla_w.desc: 3D wing lift curve slope (Helmbold formula). Determines lift sensitivity to angle of attack.
aero.out.eta_af.desc: Profile aerodynamic efficiency (Cl_α / 2π). Shows proximity to thin airfoil theory limit.
aero.out.k.desc: Induced drag factor (k = 1/(π e AR)). Determines drag increase with angle of attack in the formula CD = CD0 + k·CL².
aero.out.ld_max.desc: Maximum aerodynamic efficiency of the aircraft (1 / (2·√(CD0·k))). Indicates how far it can glide per unit of altitude loss with the motor off; 12-16 is excellent.
aero.out.oswald_e.desc: Hoeker empirical aspect ratio efficiency factor (1/(1.05 + 0.007π·AR)). Used as factor in induced drag calculation; typical 0.75-0.85.
aero.out.v_end_free.desc: Theoretical minimum power speed without stall limit.
aero.out.v_endurance.desc: Minimum power speed (CL = √(3CD0/k)). Limited to 1.2·V_stall lower bound for safety margin.
aero.out.v_range.desc: Optimum cruise speed for maximum distance per unit battery energy (CL = √(CD0/k)).
aero.out.v_stall.desc: Aircraft stall speed in cruise. Maximum 10.0 m/s recommended for safe landing and hand launch; if higher, increase wing area.

aeros.learn.camber.body: Camber is the curvature of the airfoil's mean line. A cambered airfoil gives more lift at the same angle and lets you fly slower, but adds some drag and a nose-down pitching moment.
aeros.learn.camber.exp: In the wing step, going from a 2% to a 4% cambered airfoil lowers the stall speed.
aeros.learn.camber.title: Airfoil camber
aeros.learn.drag.body: Drag is the force that holds the aircraft back. It splits into skin friction (wetted area and roughness), form drag (body shape) and induced drag, the price of lift.
aeros.learn.drag.exp: Reduce the fuselage diameter: drag drops and L/D rises.
aeros.learn.drag.title: Drag
aeros.learn.intro: A short explanation, a drawing and a small experiment for each concept.
aeros.learn.ld.body: L/D is lift divided by drag. With the motor off the aircraft glides about L/D times its height; a high L/D means going farther and staying up longer.
aeros.learn.ld.exp: Change the surface from "Rough surface" to "Sanded + painted": L/D rises.
aeros.learn.ld.title: L/D (glide ratio)
aeros.learn.lift.body: Lift is the upward force made when the wing pushes air downward. When it equals the aircraft weight the aircraft stays aloft. It grows with wing area and speed.
aeros.learn.lift.exp: In the wing step, enlarge the wing area: the stall speed drops.
aeros.learn.lift.title: Lift
aeros.learn.re.body: The Reynolds number tells how "big and fast" the flow is. It is low for small, slow aircraft, so the airfoil gives less lift and friction is higher. This matters for small UAVs.
aeros.learn.re.exp: A longer wing chord (wider wing) raises the Reynolds number.
aeros.learn.re.title: Reynolds number
aeros.learn.stall.body: If the wing meets the air at too steep an angle the flow separates and lift suddenly drops: this is a stall. Below the stall speed the aircraft falls, so this speed should be low.
aeros.learn.stall.exp: A bigger wing or a more cambered airfoil lowers the stall speed.
aeros.learn.stall.title: Stall
aeros.learn.title: Learn corner

dp.input.a_launch.desc: Forward acceleration required for the aircraft after launch.

dp.input.pw_margin.desc: Safety factor added to the minimum required power (spec 1.15 = %15 margin).

dp.out.rec_max_ws_pt.desc: Allowed highest wing loading (smallest wing, lowest drag).
dp.out.rec_min_power_pt.desc: Point within allowed range requiring the smallest motor (long endurance/fuel saving focus).
dp.out.rec_pw.desc: Required power at the recommended point.
dp.out.rec_s.desc: Wing area required to provide the recommended wing loading at current launch weight.
dp.out.rec_ws.desc: Optimum wing loading recommended according to selected optimization criterion.
dp.out.v_stall.desc: Current stall speed with current wing loading. Must be below the desired limit.

dp.out.ws_max.desc: Maximum wing loading the design can have without exceeding the desired stall speed (0.5·ρ·V_stall²·CL_max).
dp.rec_criterion_explanation: Lowest power: larger wing and less motor power; highest wing loading: smaller wing and less structure/drag, but more motor power and higher stall/launch speed.
dp_crit_max_ws: Highest Wing Loading (Compact wing and wind resistance)
dp_crit_min_power: Lowest Power (Minimum motor weight and current)
dp_intro: In this step, we are overlaying flight requirements—stall speed, climb rate, turn maneuverability, and hand-launch speed—into a single W/S vs P/W constraint diagram. The optimum wing loading and minimum required power are selected here, ensuring the aircraft can safely take off and climb without motor overload.
drone_type.fixed_wing_conv.cons: - Additional fuselage and tail weight, increased wetted area, runway requirement.
drone_type.fixed_wing_conv.desc: Conventional, proven configuration with separate horizontal and vertical stabilizers.
drone_type.fixed_wing_conv.label: Fixed Wing – Conventional Tail
drone_type.fixed_wing_conv.pros: + High longitudinal/directional stability, easy setup, wide static margin tolerance.
drone_type.fixed_wing_vtail.cons: - Elevon mixer required for pitch and yaw control, control interaction is complex.
drone_type.fixed_wing_vtail.desc: Two angled tail surfaces that combine horizontal and vertical tail functions.
drone_type.fixed_wing_vtail.label: Fixed Wing – V-Tail
drone_type.fixed_wing_vtail.pros: + Lower parasite drag and weight, less affected by propeller slipstream.
drone_type.flying_wing.cons: - Narrow static margin range (%3-8), reflex wing profile requirement, stall susceptibility.
drone_type.flying_wing.desc: Compact design with no fuselage or tail, consisting only of swept wings and elevons.
drone_type.flying_wing.label: Flying Wing
drone_type.flying_wing.pros: + Very low drag, high aerodynamic efficiency, compact portable structure.
drone_type.multirotor.cons: - Much lower endurance compared to fixed wing, limited range.
drone_type.multirotor.desc: 3, 4, 6 or 8 motor configurations, no wings, vertical takeoff and hover platform.
drone_type.multirotor.label: Multirotor
drone_type.multirotor.pros: + VTOL capability, maneuverability in all directions, precise hover at a fixed point.
drone_type.vtol_quadplane.cons: - Vertical motors create dead weight and parasite drag in cruise; complex mechanical architecture.
drone_type.vtol_quadplane.desc: Hybrid platform with a fixed-wing fuselage and four vertical lift motors plus one horizontal pusher motor.
drone_type.vtol_quadplane.label: VTOL Quadplane
drone_type.vtol_quadplane.pros: + Combines runway-independent vertical takeoff and landing (VTOL) with the long-range and speed advantages of a fixed wing.
end.input.dod.desc: The portion of the battery that can be safely used (typical 0.75-0.85). A 15-20% margin is left to preserve Li-ion/LiPo cell lifespan.
end.input.eta_esc.desc: Electronic speed controller electrical transmission efficiency (%94-97).
end.input.p_hotel.desc: Power continuously consumed independent of speed: flight controller, GPS, camera, radio transmitter and servos (8-25 W).
end.out.pack_energy.desc: Total nominal energy of the battery package selected in the Weight Breakdown section (V × Ah).
end.out.total_eff.desc: Ratio of electrical energy from the battery converted to net propulsive power at the propeller (η_esc · η_mot · η_prop).
end.out.usable_energy.desc: Net energy deliverable to the motor and system at the selected DoD margin (Pack Wh × DoD).
end.table_note: Fixed power (avionics + payload) is included in every row. CL > 0.85·CL_max indicates (yellow) results near the stall limit and may be overly optimistic.
end_intro: In this step, we calculate how long and how far the aircraft can fly using the available energy in the battery. Cruise speed, best range speed, and longest loiter speed are analyzed separately. This establishes the operational radius to complete the mission flight and return safely.

geo.input.b.desc: Total wingspan from tip to tip. Typical for this class of UAVs is 1200-2000 mm. Increasing span reduces induced drag but increases wing bending stress.
geo.input.c_tail.desc: Horizontal tail mean aerodynamic chord (assumption 100 mm). Affects tail Reynolds number.
geo.input.eta_h.desc: Dynamic pressure ratio in the tail (due to wing downwash 0.85-0.95).
geo.input.l_h.desc: Distance from wing aerodynamic center to horizontal tail aerodynamic center.
geo.input.l_v.desc: Distance from wing aerodynamic center to vertical tail aerodynamic center.
geo.input.s.desc: Wing planform projected area. Directly determines wing loading and flight stall characteristics.
geo.input.s_h.desc: Total area of horizontal stabilizer (including elevator).
geo.input.s_v.desc: Area for vertical stabilizer and rudder.
geo.input.s_vtail.desc: Sum of planform area of both V panels.
geo.input.sweep_le.desc: Aft angle of wing leading edge. 0-5° for straight wing, 15-25° for flying wing.
geo.input.taper.desc: Ratio of tip chord to root chord (c_t / c_r). A value of 0.5 - 0.8 approaches the ideal elliptical lift distribution. If too small, tip chord narrows and tip stalls early.
geo.input.tc_t.desc: Tail airfoil thickness ratio (0.08-0.10 for symmetric airfoil).
geo.input.tc_w.desc: Maximum thickness-to-chord ratio of wing airfoil. Below 0.08 early stall risk at low Re, above 0.14 increases parasite drag.
geo.out.ar.desc: Wing span divided by mean chord (b²/S). Directly determines induced drag; higher AR provides less drag and higher L/D ratio. 6-10 is ideal.
geo.out.c_r.desc: Wing root chord length at fuselage junction (2S / (b(1+λ))). Reference for carbon tube and component sizing to fit the wing.
geo.out.c_t.desc: Wing tip chord (λ · c_r). Ensures tip Reynolds number stays above 100,000 and prevents tip stall; must be at least ~85 mm.
geo.out.mac.desc: Length of the Mean Aerodynamic Chord, where equivalent aerodynamic forces on the entire wing act. Fundamental reference for CG and NP calculations.
geo.out.s_h_eff.desc: Equivalent horizontal area for stability calculation (S·cos²Γ for V-tail).
geo.out.s_h_req.desc: Minimum horizontal tail area required to achieve the specified V_H target.
geo.out.s_t.desc: Wet area used in parasitic drag (CD0) calculations.
geo.out.s_v_eff.desc: Equivalent vertical area for directional stability calculation (S·sin²Γ for V-tail).
geo.out.s_v_req.desc: Minimum vertical tail area required to achieve the specified V_V target.
geo.out.s_vtail_req.desc: Minimum total V-panel area that satisfies both horizontal and vertical volume targets simultaneously.
geo.out.v_h.desc: Horizontal tail volume coefficient (S_h·l_h / (S·MAC)). Provides longitudinal stability; must be within 0.35-0.80.
geo.out.v_v.desc: Vertical tail volume coefficient (S_v·l_v / (S·b)). Provides directional (yaw/Dutch roll) stability; must be within 0.02-0.06.
geo.out.ws.desc: Ratio of total weight to wing area. Determines stall speed and hand-launch safety. For hand-launched small UAVs, 45-100 N/m² is ideal.
geo.out.x_le_mac.desc: Distance from wing leading edge to MAC root leading edge. With sweep angle, shifts aerodynamic center rearward.
geo.out.y_mac.desc: Distance of the MAC axis from the body center line.
geo.tail_tc_mismatch_warning: Warning: Calculation t/c ({0}) differs from CAD profile t/c ({1}).
geo_ar_desc: Ratio of the square of the span to the area (b² / S). Higher AR significantly reduces induced drag and increases L/D.
geo_intro: In this step we size wingspan, wing area, taper, and tail surfaces. Wing loading (W/S) determines stall speed and hand-launch safety, while aspect ratio (AR) determines glide efficiency. Tail volume coefficients (V_H, V_V) keep the aircraft stable against wind and prevent the nose from departing control.
geo_mac_desc: Equivalent rectangular wing chord length. Stability and CG calculations are expressed as percentages of the MAC.
geo_s_desc: Top-down projected area of the wing. Directly determines wing loading (W/S). As area increases, stall speed decreases, allowing slower flight.
geo_sweep_desc: Angle of the wing leading edge backwards. Used on slow UAVs to properly position the aerodynamic neutral point and centre of gravity.
geo_taper_desc: Ratio of the tip chord to the root chord. Taper reduces wing weight and approaches elliptical lift distribution; excessive taper can cause tip stall.
geo_tc_w_desc: Ratio of the maximum airfoil thickness to the chord length (typical 8-14%). Thicker profiles make it easier to insert carbon fiber spars, but increase drag.
geo_vh_desc: Capacity of the horizontal tail to provide longitudinal stability of the aircraft. For fixed-wing UAVs it should be in the range 0.35 - 0.75.
geo_vv_desc: Capacity of the vertical tail to provide directional (yaw) stability. Typical range 0.025 - 0.055.

help.aero:
# What this section does
Calculates wing lift slope, maximum lift coefficient, drag (CD0) breakdown, drag polar, stall speed, and most efficient flight speeds.

# Concepts
- CL (Lift Coefficient): Dimensionless expression of the lift produced at any moment. If CL_max is exceeded, the wing stalls (flow separates, lift drops).
- Cl_max_2d: Maximum lift coefficient of the airfoil (2-dimensional). At low Reynolds numbers this value may be optimistic; verify with XFOIL or testing for your chosen airfoil. The program uses 90% of this for 3D wings.
- CD0 (Parasite Drag): Drag independent of lift; total of friction, form factor, and wetted area of wing, fuselage, tail and other parts.
- Oswald efficiency (e): Induced drag efficiency of the wing; the closer to 1 the better. Typical 0.7-0.85.
- L/D: Ratio of lift to drag (L/D ratio). Higher values mean more efficient flight. L/D_max is achieved when parasite and induced drag are equal.
- V_stall: Lowest speed the wing can sustain. V_range: Speed for maximum range on electric aircraft. V_end: Speed requiring minimum power (longest duration); if very close to stall, limited to 1.2 × V_stall.
- Fuselage wetted area and tail chord: Left as open assumptions during validation; entered as inputs, warning texts show the difference.

# Common mistake
Only looking at the airfoil profile and forgetting drag from the fuselage and tail. On a small UAV, fuselage and tail can make up roughly a third of total CD0.
help.design_point:
# What this section does
Constraint diagram: Wing loading (W/S) on horizontal axis, power loading (P/W) on vertical axis. Each curve shows the minimum P/W required for a mission condition (cruise, climb, turn, hand-launch). Vertical line, maximum W/S limit from desired stall speed.

# How to read it
- Green area: Left of the stall limit and above all curves, i.e. slow enough to stall safely and have enough power.
- Current design point is determined by your installed motor power and wing loading. Must be inside the green area; if outside, the program shows a red warning.
- Recommended point: Determined by 'Design criterion' selection. Default 'Minimum power': the point where the required P/W is lowest within the allowed W/S range. 'Maximum wing loading': the highest W/S (smaller wing). Both points are shown on the graph.
- Design margin: Safety factor added to required power (default 1.15).
- W/S upper limit factor: If 1.0, only V_stall ≤ desired speed is checked; setting it to 0.9 leaves a 10% margin from the stall limit.

# Common mistake
Only choosing a powerful motor for speed. Climb and hand-launch often require more power than cruise; check critical limits.
help.endurance:
# What this section does
Calculates flight time and range from usable battery energy at specific speeds: longest duration speed, longest range speed, and your chosen cruise speed.

# Concepts
- Usable energy: Pack energy × depth of discharge (DOD). Discharging the battery to the end shortens life and is unsafe; 0.8 is a reasonable value.
- Fixed power (avionics + payload): Power independently of speed consumed by camera, radio, flight controller. At low speeds this can be a large portion of total power.
- Efficiencies: Motor, ESC and propeller multiplied to determine how much shaft power is drawn from the battery.
- Duration = energy / total power; Range = speed × duration.

# Comment
For duration, the speed requiring minimum power is selected; for range, the speed with highest L/D is selected. These are not the same. In observation missions (high fixed power) slightly higher cruise speed gives best range.

# Common mistake
Assuming all battery energy can be used; capacity drops in cold, and a return (reserve) margin must be left. Propeller efficiency is also fixed, it varies with speed in reality.
help.geometry:
# What this section does
Defines wing planform (top view) and tail dimensions; calculates other sections' used values such as mean aerodynamic chord (MAC).

# Concepts
- Area (S) and span (b): Wing area and tip-to-tip length. Aspect ratio AR = b² / S. As span increases, AR increases, induced drag decreases, but wing gets heavier and more bend-sensitive.
- Taper (λ): Ratio of tip chord to root chord. Used in range 0.5-1.0. If too small, tip chord becomes very short, Reynolds number at tip decreases and tip stalls early.
- Sweep angle: Backward inclination of the wing leading edge. Kept small on slow UAVs; primary purpose is to position CG and NP.
- MAC: 'Mean aerodynamic chord' of the wing. Static margin and CG calculations are expressed as percentages of the MAC.
- Wing loading (W/S): Weight divided by wing area. Higher values increase stall speed, making hand-launch harder.
- Tail volume coefficients V_H and V_V: Dimensionless numbers showing how effective the tail is relative to the wing. On small UAVs typical V_H 0.35-0.8, V_V 0.02-0.06.
- V-tail: Horizontal and vertical surfaces combined in a V shape. Equivalent areas found as S·cos²Γ (horizontal) and S·sin²Γ (vertical).
- Flying wing: Design without tail; less drag but harder stability and control (requires washout and reflex airfoils).

# Common mistake
'Longer wing is always better'. As span increases, mass, bending load, and parts count increase; also, as chord decreases Reynolds number drops.
help.mission:
# What this section does
Enter your desired altitude (height) and cruise speed; the program calculates air properties at that height (standard atmosphere, ISA).

# Concepts
- Altitude: Height above sea level. As you climb, air thins (density drops); at the same speed you get less lift and less thrust. Typical range for this project is 0-1000 m.
- Cruise speed: Normal flight speed. Lift increases with speed squared, so does drag.
- Density (ρ): Air density in kg/m³. Used in all aerodynamic calculations.
- Reynolds number (Re): Dimensionless number indicating the inertial to viscous ratio of the airflow. In small UAVs, wing Re is usually in the range 100,000 - 500,000; in this regime, airflow over the wing easily separates, making airfoil choice and surface quality critical.
- Mach number: Ratio of speed to speed of sound. Below 0.15 air is considered incompressible; this program operates on this assumption.

# Common mistake
Thinking 'higher is better'. As altitude increases, thrust and lift decrease; also regulations and radio range limits apply.
help.propulsion:
# What this section does
Provides required thrust for cruise and hand-launch, motor power, and simple propeller controls.

# Concepts
- Cruise thrust: Thrust required to overcome drag in cruise (weight / L/D).
- Static thrust: Thrust provided by propeller at rest. For hand-launch, static thrust of at least about 0.6 times the aircraft weight is recommended (thrust-to-weight ratio).
- Propeller diameter and disk area: For the same thrust, a larger diameter propeller uses less power (momentum theory). Figure of merit (FM) is the ratio of actual propeller performance to ideal (0.6-0.7).
- Propeller tip Mach limit: Speed limit for propeller tip to avoid approaching sonic speed (around 0.45 Mach).
- Recommended motor power: The larger of static and design power, multiplied by a safety factor (default 1.1).
- C ratio: Drawn current to battery capacity; the continuous current limit of the cell must not be exceeded.

# Common mistake
Choosing an over-powered motor: it gets heavier, battery drains faster, and excess current is pulled into the package. Check the requirement in this section first, then select the motor.
help.stability:
# What this section does
Finds the centre of gravity (CG), the neutral point (NP) of wing+tail, and the static margin. This is the most critical check for safe flight attitude.

# Position system (datum)
x: Positive towards tail from nose (mm). y: Positive right, z: Positive up. Also enter distance from nose to wing leading edge root; MAC leading edge is calculated from nose. Static margin and CG percentages are measured from MAC leading edge.

# Concepts
- Neutral point (NP): As long as the CG is ahead of this point the aircraft is stable; if it moves behind it, the aircraft becomes unstable and uncontrollable.
- Static margin (SM) = (NP - CG) / MAC. Conventional aircraft target 5-15%, flying wings 3-8%. Too small SM: too sensitive and dangerous; too large SM: nose heavy, increased tail load, reduced performance.
- Battery position suggestion: Solves where to place the battery to achieve the target SM. Moving the battery forward-backwards is the easiest way to adjust CG.
- Link column: If you connect a row to the Weight Summary, the mass is automatically loaded from there.

# Common mistake
Putting parts 'where they fit'. Calculate CG first; adjust with movable mass (battery). Measure CG by hand/ fingertip on the real aircraft before first flight.
help.structure:
# What this section calculates
Wing root bending moment, carbon spar strength and margin of safety.

# Concepts
- Load factor (n): How many times the aircraft's own weight it can withstand in maneuver or turbulence. Limit 3.8, ultimate load = limit × safety factor 1.5.
- Root bending moment: Rotational effect at where wing attaches to fuselage. With elliptical load distribution M = n·W·b / (3π).
- Carbon spar stress: σ = M / Z (Z: section modulus). Allowable stress varies by material and manufacturer; 500 MPa is a typical ultimate value.
- Margin of safety MS = allowable / actual - 1. Less than zero is insufficient.


# Assumption
The shell is assumed not to carry bending moment; all bending is taken by the carbon spar. Fairings and shell only protect the profile.

# Common mistake
Forgetting wing attachment (tube joints, lugs); cracks usually start there. If needed, thicken the spar or add a second spar.
help.summary:
# What this section shows?
Overview of results from all sections and clear warnings. Colors: green = suitable, red = problematic, gray = info note.

# How to read it
First look at red [ERROR] lines; these show the design will not work as is. Yellow [WARNING] lines explain risks, gray [NOTE] lines explain assumptions.

# Remember
All results are preliminary design estimates. Verify with flight tests (short hop tests first, then full flight) before actual flight.
help.weight:
# What this section does
Totals the mass of all aircraft components and finds the Maximum Takeoff Weight (MTOW). Structure mass is estimated from shell area × wall thickness × material density; battery pack is built from cell series/parallel based on the cell table.

# Concepts
- MTOW: Total mass at liftoff. Here it is the sum of all parts; if result is larger than target, wing area, battery, and structure need re-evaluation.
- Series (S) / Parallel (P): Connecting cells in series increases voltage (approx. 3.6 V per cell), parallel increases capacity (Ah) and current handling. 4S2P = 8 cells.
- Package multiplier factor: Added mass from cables, wire harnesses, protection circuits, and casing. Cell mass is multiplied by this factor (default 1.16).
- Wall thickness: Shell wall thickness, typically 0.4-0.6 mm.
- Internal structure factor: Extra mass from ribs and junctions (1.2-1.45).
- Density: For LW-PLA (lightweight PLA) 550-650 kg/m³ is used but not tested; adjust by weighing a manufactured test part.

# How is it interpreted?
Battery mass ratio should generally be 25-45%; too low reduces flight time, too high reduces structure and payload mass.

# Common mistake
Inflating weight 'just a bit more'. Wing loading increases, stall speed increases, hand-launch gets harder. Enter actual measured weight.
mission.out_a_desc: Rate of propagation of pressure waves (a = √(γ·R·T)). Reference in Mach number calculation.
mission.out_mach_desc: Ratio of flight speed to speed of sound (M = V / a). For small UAVs M < 0.15 is required; below this the assumption that air is incompressible is entirely valid.
mission.out_mu_desc: Molecular resistance of air to shearing motion. Calculated via Sutherland formula dependent on temperature. Affects Reynolds number by influencing boundary layer friction.
mission.out_nu_desc: Ratio of dynamic viscosity to air density (ν = μ / ρ). Shows rate of momentum diffusion.
mission.out_re_desc: Ratio of inertial forces to viscous forces (Re = ρ·V·MAC / μ). Determines airfoil efficiency and laminar/turbulent flow regime. Below 100,000 laminar bubble risk and early stall increase; increase speed or chord.
mission.out_re_item_desc: Local Reynolds number based on characteristic length and cruise speed of a component. Directly used to calculate parasite drag coefficient (Cf).
mission.out_re_tip_desc: Reynolds number at the wing tip chord. To prevent early tip stall and sudden spin risk, it should be at least 100,000. If lower, increase tip chord (λ) or wingspan.
mission.out_rho_msl_desc: Standard air density at 0 m altitude (1.225 kg/m³). Referenced for validating launch and climb conditions in the most challenging circumstances.
mission_a_desc: Speed of propagation of sound waves in flight (a = √(γ·R·T)). Used to calculate Mach number. Approximately 340 m/s at sea level.
mission_alt_desc: Flight altitude above sea level. Valid range 0-11000 m; typical 0-1000 m for hobby and small UAVs. As altitude increases, air density decreases and the speed required to produce the same lift increases.
mission_intro: In this step we define the UAV's flight envelope and target cruise speed. These values calculate air density, speed of sound, and Reynolds number during flight using the ISA standard atmosphere model. All lift, drag, and power calculations for proper aerodynamic design are based on these atmospheric parameters.
mission_mach_desc: Ratio of velocity to speed of sound (M = V / a). Air compressibility is neglected and sound speed effects can be ignored as long as M < 0.3.
mission_mu_desc: Internal friction resistance of air against shearing flow. Calculated via Sutherland formula dependent on temperature. Appears in the denominator of the Reynolds number; affects boundary layer thickness and friction coefficient.
mission_p_desc: Static air pressure in the flight phase. Barometric altimeters measure this pressure difference to calculate altitude. 101325 Pa at sea level, approximately 95460 Pa at 500 m.
mission_q_desc: Kinetic pressure generated by the air flow (q = ½·ρ·V²). Lift and drag forces are directly proportional to q multiplied by wing area.
mission_re_desc: Ratio of inertial forces to viscous forces over the mean aerodynamic chord (MAC). At low Reynolds numbers (< 200,000), airfoils tend to stall early and laminar separation bubble risk arises.
mission_rho_desc: Mass per unit volume of the air. All aerodynamic lift and drag forces are directly proportional to density. As altitude increases, air thins; to produce the same lift, the aircraft must fly faster.
mission_t_desc: Standard atmospheric temperature in the flight phase (T = T0 - L·h). Determines air density and speed of sound. As altitude increases, air cools. Winter or high altitude affects battery performance and motor cooling.
mission_v_cr_desc: The target cruise speed the aircraft will use for level flight. Lift and parasite drag vary with the square of this speed. Typical 14-22 m/s (50-80 km/h) for small fixed-wing UAVs.
mr.adjacent_spacing.desc: Distance between two motors side-by-side (D_frame · sin(π/n)). The propeller diameter must be smaller than this to prevent collisions.
mr.arm_length.desc: Free arm length from the center plate to the motor.
mr.batt_pack.desc: Total battery weight including cells, cables, and enclosure.
mr.cg.calc_cg.desc: The actual mass centre found by the weighted average of components, frame, and motors.
mr.cg.datum: Datum: Frame centre (0, 0). x: forward (+), y: right (+) mm.
mr.cg.geom_center.desc: The geometric symmetry centre relative to the frame's longitudinal axis.
mr.cg.heading: Multirotor CG & Balance
mr.cg.intro: In this step we check the UAV's centre of gravity distance to the motor's geometric symmetry centre (within a %3 limit). An off-centre CG can cause some motors to overheat and burn prematurely, and the flight controller to struggle. Ensuring equal loading for all motors is achieved by adjusting positions from the component list.
mr.cg.note: Note: Frame (0,0) and all motors are automatically added symmetrically in arm coordinates.
mr.cg.title: CG & Balance
mr.cg_offset.desc: How far the CG is from the motor symmetry centre. Must not exceed %3; if exceeded, motors run unevenly, shift components towards the centre.
mr.coax_kappa.desc: Coaxial pair power interference factor κ_int (assumption 1.28; verify with measurement).
mr.cruise_power.desc: Rough estimate; level flight, f = equivalent flat plate area assumption.
mr.cruise_time.desc: Duration of forward flight until battery depletion.
mr.disk_loading.desc: Ratio of thrust to total propeller swept area. Low disk loading (< 100 N/m²) provides high efficiency and long endurance.
mr.elec_hover_power.desc: Total hover power drawn from the battery, including motor and ESC efficiency losses.
mr.flat_plate_area.desc: Equivalent flat plate area for parasite drag (f). Default 0.01 m² for 250 class.
mr.fm.desc: Figure of Merit: Ratio of ideal actuator disk power to shaft power (typical 0.60 - 0.75).
mr.frame.heading: Frame & Propeller Geometry
mr.frame.intro: In this step we define the UAV's arm spacing, arm layout, and propeller clearance. Frame size limits the maximum propeller diameter that can rotate safely without contacting each other. Proper frame geometry guarantees mechanical rigidity and propeller clearance.
mr.frame.title: Frame & Propeller Geometry
mr.frame_size.desc: Cross distance between opposite motor axes. As the frame gets larger, larger propellers can be attached and hover efficiency increases.
mr.h_lx.desc: Distance between front and rear motors in H layout (Lx).
mr.h_wy.desc: Distance between left and right motors in H layout (Wy).
mr.hover_current.desc: Total current drawn from the battery during hover (I = P_elec / V_pack). The cell's continuous current rating must not be exceeded.
mr.hover_throttle.desc: Approximate stick position required to hover. Since thrust scales with motor speed squared, throttle_hover ≈ √(1/TW) as a rough estimate (dependent on motor curve; warning issued if exceeding %60 causing excessive heating).
mr.hover_thrust_motor.desc: The pulling force a single motor must produce for the drone to hover (W / n_eff).
mr.hover_time.desc: The net time the battery can provide sustained hover (E_usable / (P_hover + P_avionics)).
mr.ideal_power.desc: The theoretical minimum power required to accelerate an air mass downwards in a frictionless environment, according to momentum theory.
mr.layout_h_only_4_arms: H layout can only be used with 4-arm frames.
mr.mass.esc.desc: Individual ESCs or 4-in-1 electronic speed controllers mass.
mr.mass.fc.desc: Flight controller board, GPS antenna, PDB and radio receiver hardware.
mr.mass.frame.desc: Total weight of carbon fiber body plates, arms, screws and landing gear.
mr.mass.heading: Multirotor Weight Summary
mr.mass.intro: In this step, we sum the masses of the frame, motors, ESCs, flight controller, battery package and payload. The total takeoff weight (MTOW) directly determines the motor power needed to hover. The battery's share of total mass (%30-50) balances flight duration versus agility.
mr.mass.misc.desc: Power cables, XT60 connector, velcro straps and LED lighting.
mr.mass.motor.desc: Net mass of a single brushless motor with its wires.
mr.mass.payload.desc: FPV camera, HD action camera or sensor payload.
mr.mass.title: Multirotor Weight Summary
mr.max_prop_size.desc: Maximum propeller diameter that can be mounted without touching each other given this frame geometry.
mr.motor_thrust_max.desc: Maximum static thrust a single motor produces at 100% throttle. Determines thrust-to-weight ratio.
mr.mtow.desc: Minimum vertical thrust force required for the entire drone to take off.
mr.plate_radius.desc: Radius of the center carbon fiber / plastic body plate.
mr.profile_power_ratio.desc: Ratio of rotor blade profile drag power to hover shaft power (default 15%).
mr.prop_clearance.desc: Minimum safety gap between tips of adjacent propellers (at least 10 mm recommended).
mr.range.desc: Range derived from cruise speed multiplied by duration, and numerically calculated maximum cruise speed.
mr.range.heading: Battery & Duration & Range
mr.range.intro: In this step we calculate total hover endurance and forward cruise range by selecting battery cell count and series/parallel configuration. During forward cruise, approximately 85% of hover power is consumed due to translational lift effect. Battery discharge current is validated against total motor current demand.
mr.range.title: Battery & Duration
mr.shaft_power.desc: Mechanical shaft power demanded from the motor after profile drag (P_ideal / FM).
mr.thrust.heading: Motor & Thrust (Momentum Theory)
mr.thrust.intro: In this step we calculate maximum motor thrust and ideal and electrical hover powers based on actuator disk momentum theory. Thrust-to-weight ratio (T/W ≥ 2.0) ensures rapid acceleration and wind resistance. Disk loading determines the aerodynamic efficiency of the propellers. Keeping hover throttle below 50% prevents motor overheating.
mr.thrust.title: Motor & Thrust
mr.total_motors.desc: Physical motor count and effective thrust factor after coaxial losses.
mr.tw_ratio.desc: Ratio of maximum thrust to takeoff weight. Minimum 1.6, ≥ 2.0 for general use, ≥ 3.0 for racing recommended.
mr.v_cruise.desc: Cruise speed during forward flight (default 12 m/s ≈ 43 km/h).
mr_cg_table_desc: Datum: Frame centre (0, 0). x: forward (+), y: right (+) mm.
mr_coaxial: Coaxial (2 motors per arm, top and bottom)
prop.d_prop_unusual_warning: Propeller diameter outside 180-300 mm (7-12 in) range; unusual for this class of UAV.
prop.input.d_prop.desc: Total span of the propeller. As diameter increases, disk loading decreases and static thrust efficiency improves.
prop.input.fm.desc: Static efficiency of the propeller according to ideal momentum theory (0.60-0.70).

step_intro_heading: What we are doing here and why?
step_why_aero: In this step, we calculate the 3D wing lift slope (CLα), zero-lift drag (CD0), and induced drag factor (k). These coefficients determine the aircraft's L/D ratio and the total resistance the motor must overcome in cruise. The aircraft's safe cruise without stalling is guaranteed by this polar curve.
step_why_design_point: In this step, we plot flight requirements—stall speed, climb rate, turn maneuver, and hand-launch—on a single constraint diagram (W/S vs P/W). The optimum wing loading and minimum required power are selected where all constraints are satisfied simultaneously. This ensures the aircraft can take off and climb safely without motor overload.
step_why_endurance: In this step, we calculate how many minutes the aircraft can stay airborne and how many kilometers it can travel using the available energy in the battery. Cruise speed, best range speed, and longest endurance (loiter) speed are analyzed separately. This allows you to determine the operation radius to complete the mission and return safely.
step_why_geometry: In this step, we dimension the wing span, wing area, taper, and tail surfaces. Wing loading (W/S) determines stall speed and hand-launch safety, while aspect ratio (AR) determines cruise efficiency. Tail volume coefficients (V_H, V_V) ensure the aircraft remains stable in wind and the center of gravity does not go out of control.
step_why_mission: In this step, we define the UAV's mission altitude and cruise speed. These values calculate the air density, speed of sound, and Reynolds number on the wing during flight using the ISA standard atmosphere model. All lift, drag, and power calculations for a proper aerodynamic design are based on these atmospheric parameters.
step_why_mr_battery_loiter: In this step, we calculate the total hover endurance and forward flight range by selecting the battery cell model and series/parallel configuration. In forward flight, approximately 85% of hover power is consumed due to translational lift effects. The battery discharge current is verified against the total current demand of the motors.
step_why_mr_cg: In this step, we control the distance of the aircraft's center of gravity from the geometric symmetry center of the motors (%3 limit). An aft center of gravity can cause some motors to overheat and wear out prematurely, and the flight controller to struggle. Balancing the components ensures equal loading on all motors.
step_why_mr_propulsion: In this step, we calculate ideal and electrical hover thrust using the motors' maximum thrust and actuator disk momentum theory. The thrust-to-weight ratio (T/W ≥ 2.0) determines rapid escape and wind resistance, while disk loading determines propeller aerodynamic efficiency. Keeping hover throttle below %50 prevents motor overheating.
step_why_propulsion: In this step, we match the motor, propeller diameter, propeller pitch, and ESC power system for hand-launch and cruise conditions. Static thrust ensures the aircraft accelerates without hitting the ground immediately after hand-launch, while pitch ensures sufficient pull is produced at cruise speed. Here, we also check if the battery can withstand the peak current drawn.
step_why_stability: In this step, we calculate the aircraft's neutral point (NP) and the actual centre of gravity (CG) with the weighted average of all components. The static margin (SM = (NP - CG)/MAC) determines the aircraft's longitudinal stability; the green band (%5-15) ensures the aircraft can fly hands-free. The ideal millimetric position of the battery inside the fuselage is automatically solved in this step.
step_why_summary: In this step, we review all critical outputs of the design, the mass breakdown, the constraint graph, and a scaled live 2D schematic together. All engineering checks (errors and warnings) are validated to approve the aircraft for production and flight.

wizard.step.endurance.what_why: In this step we calculate how long the aircraft can stay airborne and how far it can fly using the available energy in the battery. Cruise speed, best range speed and longest loiter speed are analyzed separately. This reveals the operational radius needed to complete the mission and return safely.

Static thrust ensures the aircraft accelerates without hitting the ground immediately after release, while pitch provides sufficient pull for cruise speed. wizard.step.stability.title: Centre of Gravity & Stability
wizard.step.stability.what_why: In this step we calculate the aircraft's neutral point (NP) and the actual centre of gravity (CG) weighted by all components' masses. Static margin (SM = (NP - CG)/MAC) determines the aircraft's longitudinal stability; the green band (%5-15) ensures hands-off straight flight. The battery's ideal millimetre-level position within the fuselage is solved automatically in this step.
wizard.step.structure.title: Structure
wizard.step.structure.what_why: In this step, we check the bending moment acting on the wing root and the carbon tube stress in maneuver and wind gusts (n_limit · FS). The tube's margin of safety (MS > 0) is verified.
wizard.step.summary.title: Design Summary & 2D Scheme
wizard.step.summary.what_why: In this step we review all critical outputs of the design, mass breakdown, constraint diagram, and scaled live 2D schematic together. All engineering checks (errors and warnings) are validated to confirm the aircraft is ready for production and flight.
wizard.step.weight.title: Weight Breakdown
wizard.step.weight.what_why: In this step we sum payload, avionics, propulsion, battery pack, and fuselage/wing masses. Total takeoff weight (MTOW) directly dictates the required wing area and motor power for keeping the aircraft airborne. The battery's share of MTOW (%25-45) establishes the critical balance between range and agility.

struct.spar_guide_text:
• Placement: Carries the main wing bending load; positioned along the span at maximum airfoil thickness (typically ~25–30% chord).
• Tube type: Pultruded carbon tubes provide maximum bending stiffness (~120 GPa). Roll-wrapped tubes offer superior crush and torsional resistance (~70 GPa).

mr_struct.why_heading: Why Arm Stiffness and Resonance Analysis?
mr_struct.why_text_1: • Stiffness dominates over strength: Carbon tubes rarely fail from static bending; they fail dynamically from insufficient stiffness. Excessive flex produces gyro vibration noise and PID oscillations.
mr_struct.why_text_2: • Carbon tube types: Pultruded (longitudinal fibers) tubes have the highest bending stiffness (~120 GPa). Roll-wrapped (cross-ply) tubes offer higher clamp torque and torsional resistance (~70 GPa).
